Q1: It means you tried to grant a level the user already holds, or a greater one. No remediation is needed; the user already has that access.
Q2: You need model admin access on that model, or controller superuser access.
Q3: A caller with model admin access on the model the offer belongs to, or controller superuser access.
Q4: The permission record is deleted outright. Revoking read removes the grant, the same write as taking a level back to read.
Q5: No. The error is `user is the last model admin for 1 or more models`; first grant admin on the model to another user.
Q6: Ten level-object combinations are valid. For an offer the valid levels are read, consume and admin.
Q7: It is the greater of their own grants and the grants of `everyone@external`, resolved on each check with nothing stored or cached.
Q8: No. Granting or revoking cloud access for yourself gives the error `cannot change your own cloud access`; ask another cloud admin or a controller superuser.
Q9: The pair of object and user: a unique index allows exactly one permission per user per object.
Q10: If Juju has not seen the external user yet, the grant creates that user as a side effect so the record has someone to name.
Q11: No. The access domain exposes no change streams; user and permission changes are read on demand.
Q12: The `jaas_access_controller` resource (and `jaas_access_cloud` for clouds) manages controller access, and they apply when using JAAS.
Q13: The client refuses it with the error `You have specified a controller access permission "<level>"...`; name a model or offer level, or drop the model or offer.
